design.routeDecision: Cross to the far rail or turn back to the near rail?
design.lesson: Reaching reclaimed ground secures a live line; empty regions fill.
design.counterplay: Watch each keeper before departing; close early when its path threatens the line.
design.captureConsequence: One keeper retains only the region it occupies at closure.
design.memorableMoment: The first enclosure reveals a broad part of the horizon.
design.mastery: Close a cut without losing a life.

topology.assumption: Static wall connectivity and initial enemy retention only; not a solution, timing or enjoyment proof.

background.alt: Two coastal landing decks and study huts face a sheltered teal bay beneath a distant stone causeway.

design.routeDecision: Connect the islands together, or establish opposite return routes first?
design.lesson: Both craft can build a shared route network from separate foundations.
design.counterplay: Watch the two keepers; cover different approaches and close onto reclaimed ground or meet both moving heads.
design.captureConsequence: A bridge may secure only its line while keepers occupy both sides. The new link still gives both craft a shorter return.
design.memorableMoment: Two isolated starting islands become a shared launch corridor.
design.mastery: Both craft contribute a closure before the shared clear, without a knockdown.

design.routeDecision: Bank the nearby island for a reliable start, or take the longer outside return to claim a wider region before the opponent?
design.lesson: A competitive time trial offers a short reliable bank and a longer high-value opening; both players receive the same course.
design.counterplay: Watch the keeper above each shelf; use either foundation to shorten an unfinished cut. The middle wall never banks a line.
design.captureConsequence: A conservative first enclosure creates safe staging ground; a successful longer route can overtake that head start.
design.memorableMoment: The two racers reach different amounts of safe territory from different opening commitments.
design.mastery: Complete the same course using both the conservative and long-return openings without losing a life.

brief.name: Orchard return lanes
brief.decision: Bank the short middle cut, then choose the upper western entrance or the lower eastern entrance to reach the required far-side marker.
brief.difference: Long staggered partitions create opposite entry directions; the required eastern capture prevents a near-side-only clear.
brief.artBrief: A high-angle orchard loading yard: three irregular apricot terraces, a small eastern packing shed and a curved irrigation pond, with a low morning sun. No watchtower, courtyard or skyline reused from another mission.
